title: Getting Started with MultiStateTMLE
text: start modelling hazard event. fit_initial() takes one formula per event, event left-hand side covariates right. another event appears covariate, enters number events far. death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness, death hazard therefore depends whether patient fallen ill: default hazard Cox model, death hazard \begin{aligned}     \lambda_{\text{death}}(t) = \lambda_0(t) \exp\big(      & \beta_1 \, \text{biomarker} + \beta_2 \, \text{treatment} \\      & + \beta_3 \, \text{illness}(t) \big),   \end{aligned} \text{illness}(t) 1 patient fallen ill 0 . argument tau = 1 sets time horizon, estimates refer happened time 1. events data need model, including censoring. plain formula shorthand hazard_model(formula). hazard_model() also arguments limit, maximum number events per patient (one illness ), at_risk, condition ~ illness == 0 specifying patients risk.
code: models <- list(   hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),   death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,   censoring ~ biomarker ) fit <- fit_initial(illness_death, models = models, tau = 1) fit #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE       1 #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE      NA #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA

title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_estimate() targets initial fit estimate target, risk(death), stochastic intensity intervention: fixed scaling intensity process, scale_intensity(illness = 0.5), one calibrated bring exposure given value, calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate standard error efficient influence curve. intervention_curve() traces target responds exposure grid scalings, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness raises risk death, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package, whose output fit_initial() takes .
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 )  tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), scale_intensity(illness = 0.5)) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) #> #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.2906665 0.03341164 0.2251809 0.3561521 #> #> Initial estimate: 0.2907; no targeting needed, as it already solves the EIC equation

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
code: # Illness-death data: illness is an illness that can occur once, death ends # follow-up, and so does censoring. One row per event: head(illness_death) #>   id      time     event  biomarker treatment #> 1  1 2.8926838 censoring  0.2724785         1 #> 2  2 0.1282264   illness  0.3572619         0 #> 3  2 1.2558891     death  0.3572619         0 #> 4  3 0.6567113     death -0.8616620         0 #> 5  4 0.1752960   illness  0.8083350         1 #> 6  4 0.2409278     death  0.8083350         1  # One hazard model per process. The death hazard depends on whether the # individual has fallen ill, and the illness can occur at most once: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 ) fit #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE       1 #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE      NA #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA  # The process types are inferred from the data, and the hazard models are # kept for reference: fit$processes #>         name     type                                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE       1 #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE      NA #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA fit$models$death #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness  # With a baseline treatment, a treatment model prepares estimates under # both arms, for `a` in tmle_estimate(): fit_treated <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = treatment ~ biomarker ) fit_treated #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE       1 #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE      NA #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA #>  #> Treatment model: treatment ~ biomarker, prepared for arms a = 0, 1  # \donttest{ # Data simulated with simevent can be passed as is. Here relapse is # recurrent, and the death hazard grows with the number of relapses so far. # factor(pmin(relapse, 3)) gives an effect of each count up to 3, so 3 # relapses are tracked: if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {   model <- simevent::sim_model(     biomarker = simevent::sim_covariate(function(N) rnorm(N)),     relapse = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.6, nu = 1),     death = simevent::sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     censoring = simevent::sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     effects = list(       simevent::sim_effect(relapse ~ biomarker, coef = 0.5),       simevent::sim_effect(death ~ relapse, coef = 0.4)     )   )   relapses <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 200, seed = 1)    fit_initial(     relapses,     models = list(       relapse ~ biomarker,       death ~ biomarker + factor(pmin(relapse, 3)),       censoring ~ biomarker     ),     tau = 2   ) } #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 2 #>  #>         name      type                                        model at_risk #>       <char>    <char>                                       <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   relapse recurrent                          relapse ~ biomarker   FALSE #> 2:     death  terminal death ~ biomarker + factor(pmin(relapse, 3))   FALSE #> 3: censoring  terminal                        censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE #>    tracked #>      <int> #> 1:       3 #> 2:      NA #> 3:      NA # }

title: Specify the hazard model of an event process — hazard_model
code: # A plain formula in fit_initial()'s `models` is short for # hazard_model(formula): hazard_model(death ~ biomarker + illness) #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + illness  # An illness that can happen at most once: hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker, limit = 1) #> Hazard model: illness ~ biomarker #>   limit: 1  # A relapse that can happen at most twice, and only before death of # another cause, w: hazard_model(relapse ~ biomarker, limit = 2, at_risk = ~ w == 0) #> Hazard model: relapse ~ biomarker #>   limit: 2 #>   at risk while: w == 0  # Death depending on having had two or more relapses. As in any R model # formula, wrap arithmetic and comparisons in I(): hazard_model(death ~ biomarker + I(relapse >= 2)) #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + I(relapse >= 2)  # Death depending on whether the illness came after time 0.5: hazard_model(death ~ biomarker + illness + I(event_time(illness, 1) > 0.5)) #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + illness + I(event_time(illness, 1) > 0.5)  # Death depending on whether the first relapse or illness, whichever came # first, came after time 0.5: hazard_model(death ~ biomarker + I(event_time(c(relapse, illness)) > 0.5)) #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + I(event_time(c(relapse, illness)) > 0.5)  # Use them in fit_initial(), mixed with plain formulas: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 ) fit$processes #>         name     type                                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE       1 #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE      NA #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA

title: Stochastic intensity interventions — interventions
text: scale_intensity() fixed intensity-scaling intervention: multiplies intensity named process factor alpha, \(\Lambda^z \mapsto \alpha \Lambda^z\). alpha = 1 intervention, alpha < 1 attenuates process alpha > 1 intensifies . calibrate() calibrated intervention: intensity process exposure scaled alpha brings exposure value given toward. target composite parameter, whose standard error accounts alpha estimated. calibration rules : level(theta): exposure equals theta. absolute_change(delta): exposure delta plus value without intervention. relative_change(rho): exposure rho times value without intervention.

title: Stochastic intensity interventions — interventions
code: # Fixed intensity scalings. Halve the intensity of illness, remove illness # altogether, or double it: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) scale_intensity(illness = 0) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0) scale_intensity(illness = 2) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 2)  # A time-varying scaling: halve the intensity of illness before time 0.5 # only. scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1))  # A scaling that depends on a baseline covariate: halve it only for # individuals with biomarker > 0. scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1))  # A scaling that depends on the number of events so far: halve the # intensity of a recurrent process until its first event only. scale_intensity(relapse = ~ ifelse(relapse == 0, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(relapse = ~ifelse(relapse == 0, 0.5, 1))  # Several processes at once: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5, death = 0.8) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5, death = 0.8)  # Calibrated interventions, scaling the intensity of illness so that its risk # equals 0.1, falls by 0.05, or falls to 80% of its value without # intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) calibrate(risk(illness), absolute_change(-0.05)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), absolute_change(-0.05)) calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8))  # Use them in tmle_estimate(): fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 ) tmle_estimate(   fit,   risk(death),   scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) ) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) #>  #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3053054 0.03359683 0.2394568 0.3711539 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.3053; no targeting needed, as it already solves the EIC equation # \donttest{ tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1))) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se     lower     upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:    alpha 0.2176164 0.02987141 0.1590696 0.2761633 #> 2:    theta 0.1000000 0.00000000 0.1000000 0.1000000 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se    lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.2607342 0.03592421 0.190324 0.3311443 0.03559196 # }

code: # Whether treatment is stopped: stop events (stop) set it to 1, and # restart events (restart) set it back to 0: state_variable(start = 0, stop = 1, restart = 0) #> State variable starting at 0 #>   after stop: 1 #>   after restart: 0  # The number of stops, counted up to 3: state_variable(start = 0, stop = \(s) pmin(s + 1, 3)) #> State variable starting at 0 #>   after stop: function (s) pmin(s + 1, 3)  # \donttest{ # Treatment that is stopped and restarted, any number of times, with a # death hazard that is higher while off treatment: if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {   model <- simevent::sim_model(     biomarker = simevent::sim_covariate(function(N) rnorm(N)),     stop = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.8, nu = 1),     restart = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.8, nu = 1),     death = simevent::sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     censoring = simevent::sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     effects = list(       simevent::sim_effect(stop ~ biomarker, coef = 0.5),       simevent::sim_effect(death ~ (stop - restart), coef = 1),       # Stops only while on treatment, restarts only while off it:       simevent::sim_effect(stop ~ (stop != restart), coef = -1e5),       simevent::sim_effect(restart ~ (restart != stop - 1), coef = -1e5)     )   )   treatment <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 200, seed = 1)    # Whether an individual is off treatment is the state variable off:   fit <- fit_initial(     treatment,     models = list(       hazard_model(stop ~ biomarker, at_risk = ~ off == 0),       hazard_model(restart ~ biomarker, at_risk = ~ off == 1),       death ~ biomarker + off,       censoring ~ biomarker     ),     tau = 2,     state_variables = list(       off = state_variable(start = 0, stop = 1, restart = 0)     )   )   print(fit)    # A stop leads to a state with off = 1, and a restart to one with   # off = 0:   print(fit$depend_matrix)    tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death)) } #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 2 #>  #>         name      type                   model at_risk tracked #>       <char>    <char>                  <char>  <lgcl>   <int> #> 1:      stop recurrent        stop ~ biomarker    TRUE       0 #> 2:   restart recurrent     restart ~ biomarker    TRUE       0 #> 3:     death  terminal death ~ biomarker + off   FALSE      NA #> 4: censoring  terminal   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE      NA #>  #> off: State variable starting at 0 #>   after stop: 1 #>   after restart: 0 #>     stop restart   off state s.stop s.restart #>    <int>   <int> <num> <int>  <int>     <int> #> 1:     0       0     0     1      2         1 #> 2:     0       0     1     2      2         1 #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> without intervention #>  #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.4330546 0.03952905 0.3555791 0.5105301 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.4331; no targeting needed, as it already solves the EIC equation # }
